names.note: Name page 13455 of days.pravoslavie.ru is «Святитель Филарет (Гумилевский), архиепископ Черниговский и Нежинский»; «Святитель» and the see are stripped and the surname the calendar keeps in parentheses stays. The day line gives the genitive «Филарета, архиеп. Черниговского». `fk.mjs` on the stored string returns NONE, and a Cyrillic grep for «Гумилевск» over every `saint.json` returned nothing — the seven existing Philaret folders are a fold this form stays clear of. THE DISPLAY NAME DELIBERATELY DROPS THE SURNAME: `Philaret (Gumilevsky)` as a display name already stands in the prose of `abraham-the-industrious-of-the-caves`, which cites him as the archbishop who explained that saint’s epithet, and `tests/related-floor.test.mjs` would then have demanded a `related` row in both directions for what is a citation and not a companionship. `Philaret of Chernigov` is the calendar’s own epithet, «архиеп. Черниговского», and `fk.mjs` on it returns NONE.

death.note: The day line closes «(1866)», which is the whole of what the source gives; no year of birth anywhere, and no life page behind his name.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 9 августа ст. ст. — «Свт. Филарета, архиеп. Черниговского (1866).»

attestations.note: The day's seventh entry. THE LINE AND THE NAME PAGE ARE ALL THERE IS: no life page stands behind his name. «Свт.» is `hierarch` and «архиеп.» `archbishop`, both the source's own words, and `Archbishop of Chernigov` is a key all four locale packs carry, so the see is in `office` and not only in the life. No folder held him: `ls -d saints/*gumilev*` and `ls -d saints/*humilev*` were both empty and `ls -d saints/philaret*` returned seven men, none of Chernigov. The day page prints no hymn under his name.
